newsitem.title: USA: Earth readies fleet for Martian invasion.
newsitem.headline: Earth readies fleet for Martian invasion.

text.p: The Mars Global Surveyor launched on Thursday is the first in a flotilla of robotic space craft headed for the Red Planet over the next 10 years. Here is a summary of other flights planned:

November 7 - Mars Global Surveyor, now en route to Mars, will spend one Martian year -- 687 earth days -- mapping up to 99 percent of the planet's rugged surface. Its electronic eye can spot an objects as small as a compact car.

November 16 - Russia's Mars 96 spacecraft, weighing in at six tonnes , is to be launched on a Proton rocket from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan. It is the largest of this year's planned batch of probes, and will carry 12 instruments, two landers and two spike-like surface penetrators.

December 2 - NASA's Mars Pathfinder is scheduled for launch from Cape Canaveral. It will land a mini-weather station on the surface and release a six-wheeled rover the size of an office laser printer.

The Mars Surveyor '98 spacecraft will be dispatched with an improved camera to continue the mapping of the planet from orbit. A robotic craft will touch down in the planet's southern hemisphere where it will dig trenches to look for traces of frozen underground water.
NASA plans two more probes, an orbiter and a lander. An international meeting is also set planned later this year to better define the missions. The lander may include Russian components.
NASA officials to explore the possibility of launching a remote-controlled rover that could be used to collect Martian rock samples for return to earth on a later mission.
A spacecraft may return to Earth with the samples collected by the 2003 rover for detailed analysis.
